hrv.name: Heart Rate Variability (lastNightAvg)
hrv.description: Variation between heartbeats. Higher values indicate better autonomic balance, recovery, and aerobic fitness.
hrv.typical_ranges: Adult resting: 20-80 ms. Trained runners: 50-100+. Elite endurance athletes: 100+.
hrv.interpretation: Trends matter more than absolute values. A sudden drop of 10+ ms vs personal baseline can signal accumulated fatigue, illness, or overtraining. Steady upward trend indicates adaptation.

rhr.name: Resting Heart Rate
rhr.description: Heart rate at rest. Lower values indicate stronger cardiovascular fitness.
rhr.typical_ranges: General adult: 60-100. Recreational runners: 55-70. Trained runners: 40-55. Elite endurance: 35-45.
rhr.interpretation: Sudden spike of 5+ bpm above personal baseline can signal illness, dehydration, or overtraining. Gradual decline indicates improving fitness.

sleep_score.name: Sleep Score
sleep_score.description: Composite quality score from Garmin combining sleep duration, deep/REM/light percentages, restlessness, and overnight stress.
sleep_score.interpretation: A single poor night is normal, but two or more consecutive sub-60 scores warrant easier training. Strong recovery requires consistently 70+.

total_sleep.name: Total Sleep Duration
total_sleep.description: Total time asleep (excludes time awake in bed).
total_sleep.typical_ranges: Adult target: 7-9 hours. Athletes in heavy training: 8-10 hours.
total_sleep.interpretation: Consistent sub-7-hour nights compromise recovery, glycogen replenishment, and cognitive function. Quality matters as much as quantity.

stress.name: Stress Level (daily average)
stress.description: HRV-derived continuous stress score. Reflects physiological load (training + life stress combined).
stress.interpretation: Sustained averages above 50 may indicate insufficient recovery. Elevated stress paired with low HRV strongly signals overreaching.

vo2_max.name: VO2 Max
vo2_max.description: Estimated maximum oxygen uptake during exercise. The primary ceiling for aerobic performance.
vo2_max.typical_ranges: Recreational runner: 35-50. Competitive amateur: 50-65. Elite endurance: 65-85+.
vo2_max.interpretation: Improves with consistent aerobic and high-intensity training. Updates from Garmin occur after structured outdoor runs with HR data. A 1-2 point increase per 6-12 weeks is realistic for trained athletes.

total_steps.name: Total Daily Steps
total_steps.description: All steps recorded during the day, including non-running movement.
total_steps.typical_ranges: General health target: 10,000+. Active runners often log 12,000-18,000 on training days.
total_steps.interpretation: Useful as a non-running activity proxy. Drops on rest days are expected; consistent low totals can signal sedentary behaviour or illness.

active_minutes.name: Active Minutes
active_minutes.description: Time spent in moderate or vigorous intensity activity.
active_minutes.typical_ranges: WHO target: 150 min/week moderate or 75 min/week vigorous.
active_minutes.interpretation: Tracks adherence to baseline activity guidelines. Running days will dominate this metric for trained athletes.

total_kcal.name: Total Daily Calories
total_kcal.typical_ranges: Sedentary adult: 1500-2200. Active runner: 2200-3500. Heavy training days: 3500+.
total_kcal.interpretation: Useful for nutrition planning. Days with long runs or hard workouts should see significant spikes vs baseline.
